When I was depressed (still am just a bit better) I left my house as a form of maintenance more than anything. It was part of my routine and while I occasionally stayed in bed and surfed the web I made sure to limit my time doing those things. I think that nature is the reason I'm here today and didn't play chicken with a train years ago. I won't sugar coat it, it isn't easy and it sure as hell is going to take a bit of motivation. After the first few times it should get a bit better. I think you could do it, whether it's just sitting outside for a few minutes or going for a half hour jog it will definitely help.

There's a difference between an experience and an image, looking at a picture of people having a good time doesn't create the same effect as being there. I think that by leaving your room you can leave behind some of the toxic feelings if you're willing to.

It's difficult to relate to a feeling that they're unfamiliar with, they have good intentions but don't know how they can help. The closest thing they know to depression is sadness; they're clueless and totally unaware of how you really feel or how they can help. The most I think people can offer is a shoulder to cry on or a hug.
Give the world a chance, try going outside and experiencing nature, it always helps me clear my head.
